15.Both
the issues are taken up together as they are inextricably interconnected with each other.
The onus to prove both the issues was upon the plaintiff.

It is a settled position of law that the plaintiff has to stand on its own legs in order to prove its case and the initial burden of proof is upon the plaintiff in terms of section 101 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 which is in pari materia with Section 104 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
The plaintiff has filed the present suit seeking recovery of Rs. 1,46,000/- from the defendants along with pendente lite and future interest.

It is the plaintiff's case that the plaintiff is maintaining her bank account with defendant no.1 bank and that the plaintiff had issued two cheques drawn on defendant no.1 bank i.e. cheque bearing no.
032624 and cheque bearing no. 032625 for an amount of Rs. 100/- and Rs. 110/- respectively in favour of Hyundai Motors.

The plaintiff has averred that due to the negligence, inaction and carelessness of defendant no.1 bank, an imposter changed the amount mentioned on the said cheques and entered the amount of Rs. 98,000/- and Rs. 48,000/- on the said cheques and thereby illegally withdrew a total sum of Rs. 1,46,000/- from the bank account of the plaintiff without the consent and knowledge of the plaintiff.

The plaintiff has contended that she did not fill the amount of Rs. 98,000/- and Rs. 48,000/- on the said cheques but rather she had filled an amount of 100/-
and Rs. 110/- respectively on the said two cheques but despite the same, a sum of Rs. 1,46,000/- was wrongfully debited from her bank account which has necessitated the UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.10.08 17:33:30 +05'30'
Civil Suit no. 1121/2018 Page no. 9 of 24 filing of the present suit for recovery of the said amount by the plaintiff.

16.Since the defendants in their respective written statements have categorically denied the case put forth by the plaintiff and have also denied their liability to pay any amount to the plaintiff, it was incumbent upon the plaintiff to substantiate and prove the averments put forth in the plaint and thereby give credence to its case.
In other words, the plaintiff had the onus to prove her entitlement for recovery of the alleged amount of Rs.1,46,000/- from the defendants by leading clear and cogent evidence.

In support of its case, the plaintiff has placed on record the copy of FIR no. 739/2015 Ex.
PW-1/1, copy of letter dated 12.01.2016 Ex.PW-1/2, notice dated 12.04.2016 Ex. PW-1/3, copy of mails Ex.PW-1/4, chargesheet filed by IO in FIR no. 739/15 Ex.PW-1/5, copy of cheques bearing no.
032624 and 032625 Mark A and Mark B and the copy of consumer forum order dated 25.09.2017 Mark C.
17.The

fulcrum of the case put forth by the plaintiff is that the cheques in question i.e. documents Mark A and Mark B (which were also exhibited as Ex. DW-1/3 and Ex. DW-1/4) which were purportedly issued by the plaintiff in favour of Hyundai Motors Ltd. were materially altered to the extent that the amount which was allegedly mentioned on the said cheques were changed or altered and that a total sum of Rs. 1,46,000/- was illegally deducted from the bank account of the plaintiff by an imposter in connivance the officials of the defendant no.1 bank.

It is pertinent to mention that even though the plaintiff has not specifically pleaded in the plaint that the name of the payee on the said cheques was changed or altered, it is evident from the record that the cheques in question Mark Smt. Divya Gupta vs Axiz Bank Ltd And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152799098/
6 A and Mark B bear the name of the payee as 'Rajesh UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.10.08 17:33:48 +05'30'
Civil Suit no. 1121/2018 Page no. 10 of 24 Kumar' and not Hyundai Motors Ltd. as alleged by the plaintiff.

This circumstance clearly suggests that the plaintiff also seeks to rely upon the plea of alteration as to the name of the payee on the cheques in question even though the same is not specifically averred in the pleadings.

18.To begin with, it is pertinent to mention that the plaintiff in her cross examination as PW-1 has admitted that she had signed the said two cheques in question i.e. Mark A and Mark B with her own pen and has also admitted that the dates on the said cheques were also filled by her.
Therefore, the execution of the cheques in question by the plaintiff is not in dispute and the plaintiff has herself admitted that the cheques in question were signed by her.

In this context, it is pertinent to mention that if the signature on the cheque is admitted to be that of the drawer, then the presumption as provided under Section 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is applicable and it can legally be inferred that the cheque was made or drawn for consideration on the date which the cheque bears.

Furthermore, once the execution of cheque is admitted, Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act mandates a presumption that the cheque was issued in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or other liability.

Reliance in this regard is placed on the decision of the apex court in Basalingappa vs. Mudibasappa (2019) 5 SCC 418.
19.Be that as it may, since the plaintiff has alleged that the amount as well as the name of the payee that was originally mentioned on the cheques in question was changed or altered by an imposter in connivance with the officials of the defendant no.1, the burden of proving the said assertion was squarely upon the plaintiff.

However, the plaintiff has miserably failed to substantiate and prove that any particulars whatsoever on the UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date:
2025.10.08 17:33:58 +05'30' Civil Suit no. 1121/2018 Page no. 11 of 24 respective cheques in question Mark A and Mark B were altered or were changed in any manner and consequently the plaintiff has failed to prove that any material alteration of the cheques in question had taken place pursuant to their execution and rather the plaintiff has made vague and bald assertions unsubstantiated by any cogent and credible evidence.

It is pertinent to mention that no corroborative or any cogent evidence whatsoever was lead by the plaintiff to prove that the particulars as to the amount as well as the name of the payee on the cheques in question Mark A and Mark B were altered in any manner pursuant to their execution by the plaintiff.

If the name of the payee as well as the amount mentioned on the cheques in question was indeed altered or changed as has been alleged, the plaintiff could have bought on record the copy of the said alleged cheques purportedly issued by the plaintiff or any contemporaneous record thereof so as to denote any difference in the name of the payee and the amount that was purportedly filled on the said cheques as alleged and the name of the payee and the amount as has been mentioned on the cheques in question and thereby show any material alteration in the cheques in question i.e. document Mark and Mark B.

However, the plaintiff has failed to bring any such document on record and has also failed to bring on record any cogent and corroborative evidence in support of the averments put forth in the plaint and accordingly the plaintiff has miserably failed to substantiate the allegations of alteration or tampering of the cheques in question.

7 20.Furthermore, no expert witness such as a handwriting expert or a forensic expert was examined by the plaintiff to show any overwriting, erasures or any alteration or tampering whatsoever on the cheques in question.

sentences.text: The absence of any such expert evidence in the present case is indeed UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.10.08 17:34:09 +05'30'

Civil Suit no.
1121/2018 Page no. 12 of 24 inexplicable and is a significant lacuna much so because where any material alteration of a negotiable instrument such as a cheque is alleged, the testimony and evidence of an expert witness such as a handwriting expert or a forensic expert is imperative so as to show any ink differences, erasures, overwriting or to show any evidence or proof of tampering on the said instrument as the said expert opinion is based on a scientific examination of the instrument/cheque.

Therefore, the plaintiff did not produce any corroborative or any cogent evidence whatsoever to prove the alleged alteration of the cheques in question and consequently, the plaintiff has miserably failed to prove that any particulars on the cheques in question were changed or altered in any manner.

In the absence of any such evidence, the allegation of tampering or material alteration of the cheques in question is a mere bald assertion which has remained utterly unproved and unsubstantiated and accordingly a grave doubt is cast on the veracity of the version put forth by the plaintiff as the plaintiff has merely made bald and vague assertions unsubstantiated by any cogent and credible evidence.

21.Moving further, the plaintiff has alleged that the cheques in question were encashed due to the negligence, inaction and carelessness of the officials of the defendant no.1 bank due to which the plaintiff allegedly suffered a wrongful loss of Rs. 1,46,000/- and the plaintiff has accordingly sought recovery of the said amount from defendant no.1 bank and also from defendant no.2.
This court would first proceed to determine as to whether any liability can be fastened on defendant no.1 in the present case.

To attract any liability against defendant no.1 bank in the present case, the plaintiff had to prove that defendant no.1 bank had no legal obligation to process the said cheques for payment or that defendant no.1 bank was UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date:
2025.10.08 17:34:20 +05'30' Civil Suit no. 1121/2018 Page no. 13 of 24 negligent in exercising the standard of care expected of a banker due to which the plaintiff had incurred the alleged wrongful loss.
However, the plaintiff has miserably failed to prove any liability of the defendant no.1 bank in the present case for reasons explained hereunder.
22.As already discussed, the foundation of the entire suit rests on the alleged plea of tampering or material alteration of the cheques in question Mark A and Mark B.
However, the plaintiff has not led any cogent or credible evidence to establish that the cheques in question were tampered with or that there was any material alteration of the said cheques.

Therefore, since the plaintiff has miserably failed to prove any alteration or tampering of the cheques in question and since the execution of the cheques in question by the plaintiff is not in dispute, the defendant no.1 bank being a mere intermediary and being the drawee bank had the legal duty and the obligation to process the cheques in question for their payment in due course of the banking business.

Furthermore, once the due execution of the cheques in question stands proved and the signatures on the cheques in question have also been admitted by the plaintiff to be her own, the presumptions envisaged under Section 118 and 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 operates in favour of the said cheques being validly issued for a lawful consideration and in discharge of a legally enforceable debt or liability and the same further weakens the case of the plaintiff as no evidence whatsoever was lead Smt. Divya Gupta vs Axiz Bank Ltd And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152799098/
8 by the plaintiff to rebut the said statutory presumptions.
23.Furthermore, the plaintiff has not brought any material on record to suggest that defendant no. 1 bank contravened or violated any banking procedure or that it failed to exercise any due diligence in clearing the UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.10.08 17:34:29 +05'30'
Civil Suit no. 1121/2018 Page no. 14 of 24 cheques in question or that any official of defendant no.1 bank acted in connivance with an imposter as alleged by the plaintiff and accordingly the allegations of negligence, carelessness, deficiency in services and connivance made against defendant no.1 bank are wholly unsubstantiated and are devoid of any merits.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to mention that the role of the defendant no.1 bank in the present case was that of a mere intermediary in processing and clearing the cheques in question that were issued by the plaintiff and which were presented to it for their encashment in due course of the banking business.

Therefore, in the absence of any proof of any negligence or any breach of duty on part of defendant no.1, no liability can be fastened on defendant no.1 on the basis of unsubstantiated and vague assertions.

Accordingly, the plaintiff has miserably failed to prove any negligence, deficiency in services or any connivance on part of defendant no. 1 bank and consequently no liability arises against defendant no.1 in the present case.

The defendant no.1 bank having acted within the statutory and procedural framework and having performed its duty as a mere intermediary cannot be held liable for processing and clearing the cheques in question which themselves bear the admitted signature of the drawer i.e. the plaintiff and consequently no case for any recovery is made out against defendant no.1.
24.It

now becomes imperative to examine as to whether defendant no.2/Ashish Kumar Yadav is liable to pay the amount sought to be recovered by the plaintiff in the present suit or as to whether the said defendant has incurred any liability towards the plaintiff.
It is pertinent to mention that the entire plaint is silent as to the role of defendant no.2 in the present case.

In other words, in the entire plaint, the plaintiff has not specifically mentioned or described the role of defendant no. 2 in the UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.10.08 17:34:45 +05'30'
Civil Suit no. 1121/2018 Page no. 15 of 24 alleged alteration or encashment of the cheques in question and the same is inexplicable.

The plaintiff has merely averred in a general and a vague manner that the officials of the defendant no.1 bank had leaked the balance of the plaintiff's bank account and that due to the alleged negligence, inaction, carelessness of the officials of the defendant no. 1 bank, an imposter succeeded in altering the amount on the cheques in question and thereby illegally withdrew a sum of Rs. 1,46,000/- from the account of plaintiff without the knowledge and consent of the plaintiff in connivance with the officials of defendant no.1.

Therefore, it is amply clear that the identity of the said alleged imposter has not been described or mentioned in the plaint and there is nothing in the plaint which indicates that defendant no. 2 is being described as the said alleged imposter.

The only reference to defendant no. 2 arises from the fact that the plaintiff has averred that a case under Section 420 IPC was registered vide FIR no. 739/2015 at PS Roop Nagar based on the complaint made by the plaintiff and that a chargesheet was subsequently filed against defendant no.2 by the police and that the trial of the said case is pending adjudication.

Therefore, except for the mention of the said FIR and the criminal complaint, there are no specific pleadings or averments in the plaint to suggest any act, omission or involvement of defendant no. 2 in the alleged alteration or encashment of the cheques in question.

In the absence of any specific pleadings showing the role of defendant no.2, no cause of action can be said to have accrued against defendant no. 2 in the Smt. Divya Gupta vs Axiz Bank Ltd And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152799098/

25.Be that as it may, the plaintiff has even otherwise failed to prove any liability of defendant no. 2 in the present case for reasons explained UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date:
2025.10.08 17:34:57 +05'30' Civil Suit no. 1121/2018 Page no. 16 of 24 hereunder.

It is pertinent to mention that no cogent or credible evidence was brought on record by the plaintiff to show that defendant no. 2 was in any manner connected in the alleged alteration or the encashment of the cheques in question.

Furthermore, the plaintiff has not produced any evidence whatsoever to establish that defendant no. 2 had derived any pecuniary benefit or any unjust enrichment at the expense of the plaintiff in relation to the cheques in question.

Therefore, even assuming for the sake of arguments that defendant no. 2 is the said alleged imposter, no evidence whatsoever has been led by the plaintiff to establish that defendant no.2 was connected or involved in the alleged alteration or encashment of the cheques in question nor has any proof been brought on record to show that defendant no.2 had derived any pecuniary benefit or had caused any wrongful loss to the plaintiff so as to impute any liability on defendant no.2.

Furthermore, the mere registration of an FIR against defendant no.2 or the naming of defendant no. 2 in a chargesheet pertaining to a criminal complaint cannot form the foundation to fasten any civil liability upon defendant no.2.

If the name of the payee as well as the amount mentioned on the cheques in question was indeed altered or changed as has been alleged, the plaintiff could have bought on record the copy of the said alleged cheques purportedly issued by the plaintiff or any contemporaneous record thereof so as to denote any difference in the name of the payee and the amount that was purportedly filled on the said cheques as alleged and the name of the payee and the amount as has been mentioned on the cheques in question and thereby show any material alteration in the cheques in question i.e. document Mark and Mark B.
